title: Más bien: matizar en vez de simplemente contrastar

sections.content: Más bien (rather) corrects or refines a claim instead of flatly opposing it -- useful when a reading needs to say something wasn't quite X, it was actually Y. It's gentler than sino, which requires an explicit negation just before it. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Estos regímenes no eran, más bien, una simple repetición de los golpes militares del siglo diecinueve.
items.english: These regimes weren't, rather, a simple repetition of the nineteenth-century military coups.

items.spanish: No se trataba de un caudillo gobernando solo; más bien, eran las propias fuerzas armadas tomando el poder como institución.
items.english: It wasn't a caudillo governing alone; rather, it was the armed forces themselves taking power as an institution.

items.spanish: La represión no respondía a una amenaza real, sino que se apoyaba, más bien, en una ideología que veía enemigos en toda la sociedad.
items.english: The repression didn't respond to a real threat; rather, it rested on an ideology that saw enemies throughout society.

items.spanish: El poder económico no quedaba en manos de los militares mismos, más bien se entregaba a equipos de tecnócratas civiles.
items.english: Economic power didn't remain in the hands of the military themselves; it was rather handed over to teams of civilian technocrats.

sections.content: Más bien can stand alone mid-sentence (set off by commas) or pair with no... sino que for a stronger correction. Don't confuse it with mejor dicho (rather, that is to say), which corrects your own previous wording rather than someone else's claim.
